correctness.rationale: PASS because the unique reduced rational conic parameter, the exact \(d\in\{1,3\}\) gcd lemma, the modulo-three impossibility for \(d=1\), and coprime-valuation characterization when \(d=3\) prove a disjoint exhaustive parametrization. In each of the two fixed hyperbolic wedges, area \(Y\log2/4\), residue factor \(3/(4\zeta(2))\), and lattice-slice/Möbius error \(O(\sqrt Y\log(2Y))\) give precisely \(3\log2/(4\pi^2)\sqrt X\). An independent factor-pair enumerator agrees at six exhaustive finite cutoffs; finite tests are corroboration only. Boundary: equilateral primitive triangle has perimeter three and is excluded without changing the count.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An asymptotic for all perimeters with order \(X\) does not determine a square-perimeter subfamily of order \(\sqrt X\). A broader parameterization does not imply the new sharp constant by mere substitution; two local valuation branches and a new Möbius-weighted hyperbolic lattice count are required. The inaccessible full papers are named as risks rather than declared conclusively not covering.

originality.rationale: PASS with explicit residual risk: The accessible complete Zelator and Zimhoni texts classify ambient Eisenstein triangles, but their theorems do not count primitive triangles with square perimeters or imply the sharp \(\sqrt X\) coefficient/error. Gordon–Wells studies unrestricted perimeters, a logically weaker statistic for the sparse square subset. A350038 tabulates possible perimeter values rather than triangle counts. Searches for aliases, congruence reduction, square factors, and the constant found no decisive prior coverage. Full texts of plausible older printed sources were inaccessible; an unindexed prior derivation cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: 2010 Gordon–Wells full text was not available despite its highly relevant title; unrestricted-count abstract alone does not prove noncoverage of a separately stated square-perimeter corollary.
The original printed papers of Gilder (1982), Burn (2003), and Gordon (2012) could not be inspected page by page.
An unindexed or unpublished equivalent derivation may exist; negative keyword and database searches alone never prove absolute novelty.

value.rationale: PASS because requiring the perimeter of a primitive sixty-degree integer triangle to be square is a natural invariant of a classical Diophantine family. The result proves an exact nontrivial divisibility obstruction, a unique two-family classification, and an asymptotic with explicit coefficient and nontrivial error, none provided by the general ambient parametrizations or known finite perimeter tables. It is not a mere rescaling of the recent result for right triangles: the Eisenstein norm, three-adic obstruction, and two different residue wedges are substantively different. No broader paper-sized theorem is claimed.
